text: Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Brighton and Hove Albion at Selhurst Park.
It is 15th-place Palace against ninth-place Brighton as the M23 derby takes centre stage in the Premier League today.
The Eagles are looking to end a six-match winless streak, but will have taken confidence from their comeback draw against reigning champions Manchester City last weekend.
Their opponents, meanwhile, are seeking a response to a 2-0 defeat by Arsenal last time out - their second defeat in five games.
Roy Hodgson makes three changes from the draw with City.
Ayew returns from suspension, while Lerma and Hughes are also back in the starting XI as Henderson makes his home debut between the sticks.
Riedewald and Schlupp drop to the bench, with Joel Ward missing out through injury after he was substituted in the first half at the Etihad Stadium.
The likes of Odsonne Edouard, Rob Holding and Sam Johnstone remain absent for the Eagles.
As for Brighton, Roberto De Zerbi makes four alterations from the defeat at Arsenal.
Hinshelwood, Igor, Balepa and Pedro all start with Milner, Lallana and Ferguson dropping to the bench, while Joel Veltman misses out through injury.
He joins the likes of Ansu Fati, Julio Enciso, Pervis Estupinan, Solly March, Adam Webster and Tariq Lamptey in the treatment room.
If history is anything to go by, we should be in for a closely fought encounter today.
Indeed, the last four Premier League meetings between the sides at Selhurst Park have all ended in a 1-1 draw.
The teams have made their way out onto the field and we are almost ready to go at Selhurst Park.
Referee John Brooks blows his whistle and Palace get the match under way.
Gross makes a positive run into Palace's half as he looks to connect with Pedro's attempted throughball.
However, the hosts are able to cut it out and prevent the ball from reaching the Brighton midfielder, who could well have been bearing down on goal.
Gross is involved again as he takes aim from the edge of the area after a scrappy passage of play culminates in the ball breaking kindly for him.
But he drags his effort well wide of the target.
Sunday's defeat at Arsenal ended Brighton's run of 32 successive Premier League matches in which they had scored.
The Seagulls look eager to make amends for that today.
There is a fairly subdued atmosphere at Selhurst Park, where Palace have lost each of their last four Premier League games.
The Eagles were last beaten five times on the bounce at home in the English top flight between December 2016 and February 2017.
Can Mateta make a difference for the hosts today? The striker has scored in his last two Premier League matches having failed to do so in the previous 18.
You must go back to October 2017, when he was plying his trade with Ligue 2 side Le Havre, for the last time he netted in three successive league games.
Lerma's tremendous throughball catches Brighton off-guard and releases Olise down the right wing.
He has Mateta to aim for in the box, but his cross is not the best and the visitors can eventually relax with a goal-kick.
We are still goalless after the opening quarter of an hour at Selhurst Park.
Brighton have edged the possession, but there has only been one shot on goal between the sides thus far.
Palace are the only Premier League side without a home win since the start of October.
The Eagles have only recorded a joint-low one victory overall during that time, along with Nottingham Forest and Luton Town.
GOOD SAVE! Igor's sweeping ball towards the edge of the box evades Hinshelwood and reaches Adingra, who draws a fine reflex save from Henderson.
Balepa then sends his volleyed rebound wide of the target.
Adringra's shot was the first attempt on target as we hit the midway point in the first half.
Brighton will look to use that as a platform to build on as they try to get back to winning ways.
Brighton have only lost two of their eight midweek Premier League games in 2023.
Although, both of those defeats did come away from home.
Ayew stays down in protest following an off-the-ball tangle with Hinshelwood.
It looked quite innocuous in all fairness, though, and the Palace forward is soon back on his feet.
The ball breaks kindly for Mateta, who unleashes a fierce attempt from outside the area.
Although, it is straight at Verbruggen, who gathers comfortably enough.
Mateta knocks the ball away to prevent Brighton from taking a quick free-kick.
The Palace forward subsequently receives the first yellow card of the game.
Balepa bundles over Hughes just outside the Brighton penalty area and goes into the book.
This is a dangerous position and the hosts will want to capitalise.
Palace look to threaten and force a corner.
The delivery into the box ricochets off Ayew, but Verbruggen reacts quickly to gather the loose ball.
Brighton are looking to end their wretched run of 21 successive Premier League matches without a clean sheet.
That is their longest ever streak in the league.
Danger for Brighton as Ayew drills a vicious ball into the six-yard box from the left.
However, with Mateta lurking, Van Hecke reacts quickly to intervene and clear the visitors' lines.
Palace threaten again down the left.
Olise embarks on a powerful infield run before finding Lerma, whose low cross is gathered by Verbruggen with Mateta waiting to pounce.
At the other end, space opens for Gross to try his luck from distance.
There is plenty of venom in his attempt, which Henderson is forced to push away to safety.
Palace are yet to win any of their five midweek Premier League matches in 2023, losing four.
The Eagles also failed to score in each of those defeats.
Receiving the ball out on the left flank, Gross steps inside and delivers a deep cross towards the far post.
It just evades the run of Hinshelwood before Henderson collects.
AYEW!!! 1-0 PALACE! Verbruggen's error is punished by the hosts! The Brighton goalkeeper tries to be too clever and his attempt at a lofted pass goes straight to Olise.
The latter receives a return ball from Hughes before clipping it to the far post, where an unmarked Ayew nods home from close range.
Olise demonstrated wonderful anticipation as he intercepted Verbruggen's ball.
He then showed great awareness to pick out Ayew at the far post.
HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-0 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
That goal came at an ideal time for Palace, who head into the break with the lead at Selhurst Park.
Chances had been few and far between until the first minute of stoppage time, when the hosts pounced on Verbruggen's poor clearance with Olise crossing for Ayew to break the deadlock.
Brighton controlled possession for large periods of the first half, recording 60.5 per cent of it.
But from it, they only fashioned two shots on target.
Therefore, De Zerbi will be urging his players to show more of a clinical edge upon the restart.
De Zerbi has taken action at the break by making two changes.
The first of these sees him introduce Welbeck in place of Adingra.
Buonanotte also enters the action for the hosts.
Balepa is the player to make way.
Fresh from that double-substitution, Brighton get the ball rolling again in the second half.
Palace go straight onto the attack from the restart and force a corner.
Under pressure from Lerma, Verbruggen does well to punch clear for Brighton.
Hughes trips Gross to prevent the Brighton midfielder from embarking on a potential counter.
The Palace man goes into the book for his troubles.
Brighton threaten and Welbeck helps Gross' corner towards goal.
However, Ayew is well-placed to block his header and the hosts eventually scramble the ball clear.
Buonanotte looks to get Brighton moving, but is stopped in his tracks by a combination of Mitchell and Richards.
The referee deems Mitchell's intervention the less acceptable and books the left-back.
CHANCE! Dunk pulls away from his marker to meet Gross' free-kick at the far post.
However, he sends his header wide of the right post.
Brighton want a penalty as Hinshelwood goes to ground under pressure from Ayew.
The referee consults VAR, who swiftly confirm the incident unworthy of the need for him to point to the spot.
Igor drags back Olise, who gained plenty of ground with a strong run down the right flank.
The Brighton left-back is booked.
SAVE! Buonanotte, who has been impressive since coming on, leads Brighton's charge again with a jinking run before feeding Mitoma.
The latter cuts inside and gets a shot away, but it is straight at Henderson.
Palace turn to the bench and Hughes makes way to be replaced in the middle of the park by youngster Ozoh.
Players making positive impacts from the bench is something Brighton are very accustomed to.
In fact, their substitutes have scored 10 goals in the Premier League this season - more than any other side.
Youth has certainly played its part for Brighton in 2023, with nine different teenagers representing them.
Only Tottenham (1993) and Middlesbrough (2006) have fielded more teenagers during a calendar year in the Premier League (both 10).
GOOD EFFORT! Following a decent spell of Brighton pressure, the ball bounces kindly for Gilmour to strike on the volley.
There is plenty of power in the Scotland international's strike, but Henderson is equal to it.
CHANCE! Another neat move by the visitors sees Mitoma release Gross down the left.
The latter crosses to the far post, where Hinshelwood arrives, but is unable to keep his first-time shot down from a tight angle.
A nervy moment for Palace and Henderson, who is unable to gather a cross from the left with several attempts.
However, the defence comes to his rescue as they manage to block Van Hecke's strike before clearing.
The hosts make another change and the hard-working Ayew is given a well-earned rest.
Eze takes his place for the final 20 minutes.
Henderson called into action again as he races out of goal and Pedro is eventually forced out of play.
Although, the offside flag is then raised against the Brighton forward.
Brighton continue to threaten and Gilmour whips a dangerous ball towards the far post.
Unfortunately, none of his team-mates anticipate it and the ball goes behind for a goal-kick.
De Zerbi decides youth should be substituted by experience as he withdraws Hinshelwood in favour of Lallana at right-back.
Although they lead, Palace will be wary.
Only Sheffield United (13) have conceded more goals than the Eagles (nine) in the final 15 minutes of Premier League matches this season.
GREAT BLOCK! Following a clever shimmy by Mateta, Palace can counter and Eze is free on the left.
The striker finds him, but Van Hecke gets across quickly to make a wonderful block.
JUST OVER! The hosts continue to push for the second goal, which could put the game beyond Brighton.
Andersen's precise pass finds Mateta on the edge of the box.
The forward makes a yard for himself, before rifling a fierce attempt just over from a tight angle.
Brighton half-heartedly appeal for a penalty as the unbalanced Mitoma goes to ground in the box.
The referee is not interested and the unimpressed Henderson helps the Brighton winger back to his feet.
WELBECK!!! 1-1! Brighton are level and it is a wonderful header! The visitors have been knocking at the door and they are rewarded.
Gross steps inside from the right and delivers a left-footed cross that is met by Welbeck, who beats Henderson with a brilliant looping header from near the penalty spot.
Gross showed great vision to pick out Welbeck with his cross, enabling the striker to head the visitors level.
Brighton turn straight to the bench.
Mitoma, who had been limping for several minutes, goes off to be replaced by Moder.
The visitors have their tails up and push to complete the turnaround.
Van Hecke goes to ground in the box under pressure from Guehi, but the referee is quick to wave away any penalty appeals.
Ozoh goes into the book for a foul on Moder.
The youngster will have to tread carefully for the remainder of the contest.
Brighton are looking the more likely to snatch all three points as we enter the final two minutes of regulation time.
Andersen fails to clear a hopeful ball towards Welbeck, but does well to block Pedro's subsequent attempt.
WHAT IS HE DOING?! That is a let-off for Henderson and Palace! The goalkeeper charges out to intercept a cross from the right.
But rather than catch, he looks to punch the ball clear and sends it straight into the face of Welbeck.
The ball ricochets towards the goal but, thankfully for the hosts, wide of the target.
Henderson takes a little too long with his goal-kick for the referee's liking.
The goalkeeper goes into the book as a result.
Welbeck fires over from a tight angle as we enter the first of five additional minutes at the end of this game.
Can either side find the winning goal?
Mateta attempts to rally the home fans as the clock ticks down at Selhurst Park.
Can Palace end their winless streak in the most dramatic fashion?
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-1 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
For the fifth successive Premier League meeting at Selhurst Park, Palace and Brighton play out a 1-1 draw.
Welbeck's late header rescued a point for the Seagulls after Ayew nodded the hosts in front just before half-time.
The point lifts Brighton to eighth place, while the Eagles remain 15th after stretching their winless streak to seven matches.
Palace look to stop that run when they travel to Chelsea next Wednesday, while Brighton host Tottenham the following day.
Thank you for joining us today.
Until next time, goodbye!
